title: Instagram Reels (Instagram Graph API publishing)
description: Reels published through the Instagram Graph API content-publishing endpoints. Hard limits follow Meta's published Reel specifications; no B-frames, constant frame rate and the loudness targets are conservative extras and only warn.

sources.title: Meta for Developers: Instagram Platform, IG User Media reference, Reel specifications

notes: Meta lists the audio bitrate as '128kbps' without saying whether it is a ceiling or a target. This profile treats it as a ceiling (with 2 kbps of slack for AAC overshoot) and only warns.
Meta asks for 'no edit lists'. An MP4 with B-frames normally needs an edit list to start at time zero, which is why this profile also warns about B-frames.
Instagram re-encodes every upload. Passing these checks makes rejections and processing errors unlikely; it does not guarantee how the post is ranked.

video.size.note: Not in Meta's API spec; 1080x1920 is the common full-quality vertical size.

video.cfr.note: Not in Meta's API spec; variable frame rate is a common cause of audio drift after re-encoding.

video.b_frames.note: Not in Meta's spec. Without B-frames an MP4 needs no edit list to start at time zero.

audio.bitrate.note: Meta writes '128kbps'. Treated as a ceiling with 2 kbps of slack, because AAC encoders asked for 128k often measure slightly above it.

audio.loudness.note: Common streaming target; Meta publishes no loudness requirement.

audio.hiss.note: Observed 2026-10: a heuristic calibrated on game-trailer mixes, not a platform rule; see docs/checks.md#audiohiss.
